value: Purely temporary in nature
reasoning: Classical economics holds that flexible wages and prices, together with Say's law, keep the economy at full employment, so any unemployment is a short-lived disequilibrium that the market corrects by itself.

value: More fixed capital per worker
reasoning: Capital deepening means the stock of capital grows faster than the labour force so that each worker is equipped with more capital, as against capital widening, which merely extends the existing capital-labour ratio to more workers.

value: The claim that Article 32 extends to enforcing ordinary law is incorrect
reasoning: Article 32 is itself a fundamental right and is available only to enforce the rights in Part III; a grievance under ordinary law must be taken to the High Court under Article 226 or to the appropriate court, not to the Supreme Court under this article.

value: Habeas corpus
reasoning: Habeas corpus, meaning to have the body, commands whoever is holding a person to produce them before the court, which then releases them if the detention has no legal basis.

value: To promote village and cottage industries
reasoning: Promoting cottage industries is a Directive Principle addressed to the State, not a duty of the citizen; respecting the National Flag, defending the country and providing educational opportunity to one's child between six and fourteen are all listed among the Fundamental Duties in Article 51A.

value: War, external aggression and armed rebellion
reasoning: The Forty-fourth Amendment replaced the vague ground of internal disturbance with armed rebellion, so a national emergency can now be proclaimed only for war, external aggression or armed rebellion.

value: The claim that relief lies only against the husband or male live-in partner is not true
reasoning: The Act allows an aggrieved wife or woman in a relationship in the nature of marriage to proceed against relatives of the husband or male partner as well, and the courts have read the respondent to include female relatives, so relief is not confined to the man himself.

value: The claim that NIIF and NIF are the same organisation is incorrect
reasoning: The National Investment Fund of 2005 was set up to hold the proceeds of disinvestment, whereas the National Investment and Infrastructure Fund announced in the 2015-16 Budget is a separate vehicle for raising and channelling long-term money into infrastructure.

value: The claim that it was set up by the British in the Second World War is incorrect
reasoning: The Andaman and Nicobar Command was raised in 2001 as India's first tri-service theatre command, headquartered at Port Blair under a three-star officer drawn in rotation from the three services.

value: The member who has served longest on the Committee
reasoning: The chairmanship of the Chiefs of Staff Committee rotates by seniority of tenure on the committee rather than by service, so it falls to whichever of the three service chiefs has been a member the longest.

value: An infantry regiment of the Indian Army
reasoning: The Jammu and Kashmir Rifles trace their descent from the state forces of the erstwhile princely state and were absorbed into the Indian Army as a regular infantry regiment; it is distinct from the Rashtriya Rifles and from any state police body.

value: The Army has its own Corps of Air Defence
reasoning: The Army Air Defence was separated from the Regiment of Artillery in 1994 as a corps in its own right; the Mechanised Infantry, the Corps of Electrical and Mechanical Engineers and the Army Medical and Dental Corps are likewise separate arms, not sub-divisions of the bodies named against them.

value: North Eastern Command
reasoning: The Indian Army is organised into the Northern, Southern, Eastern, Western, South Western and Central Commands together with the Army Training Command; the north-east falls under Eastern Command, and there is no separate North Eastern Command.

value: The rank of Second Lieutenant has been abolished
reasoning: Cadets are now commissioned directly as Lieutenants, the intermediate rank of Second Lieutenant having been done away with; the Chief of Army Staff holds the rank of General, Field Marshal being an honorary five-star rank, and a Lieutenant General outranks a Major General.

value: Tatra
reasoning: Tatra is the heavy all-terrain truck used to carry and launch equipment, not a missile at all, whereas Akash and Trishul are surface-to-air systems and Astra is an air-launched missile.

value: The share of the services sector has increased sharply
reasoning: India's growth has been led by services, whose share of national income has risen past half, while agriculture's share has fallen steeply and manufacturing's has stayed broadly flat rather than declining.

value: Foreign portfolio investment
reasoning: Hot money is capital that moves in and out of a country at short notice in search of quick returns, which describes portfolio flows into shares and bonds; direct investment is committed to physical assets and cannot be pulled out so easily.

value: All of them — CRISIL, CARE and ICRA
reasoning: CRISIL, CARE and ICRA are all credit rating agencies registered with the Securities and Exchange Board of India, alongside others such as India Ratings and Brickwork.

value: Y. V. Reddy
reasoning: The Fourteenth Finance Commission, constituted in 2013 and reporting for the period from 2015, was chaired by the former Reserve Bank Governor Y. V. Reddy, and it raised the States' share of the divisible pool to forty-two per cent.

value: United States, Canada and Mexico
reasoning: The North American Free Trade Agreement, in force from 1994, created a free trade area among the United States, Canada and Mexico.

value: All three — Article 17, the Protection of Civil Rights Act 1955 and the Prevention of Atrocities Act 1989
reasoning: Article 17 abolishes untouchability, the Protection of Civil Rights Act punishes its practice, and the Prevention of Atrocities Act creates special offences and courts for crimes against Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

value: The claim that the Supreme Court alone can issue writs for fundamental rights is untrue
reasoning: High Courts issue the same writs under Article 226, and on even wider grounds since that power extends beyond fundamental rights to any legal right; the original jurisdiction in federal disputes, the advisory jurisdiction and the power of review are all correctly stated.

value: Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram
reasoning: The Sixth Schedule provides for autonomous districts and regional councils in the tribal areas of these four north-eastern States; Manipur's hill areas and Arunachal Pradesh are governed under other arrangements.

value: The claim that Ninth Schedule laws become void for violating a fundamental right is incorrect
reasoning: Article 31B is a saving clause: a law placed in the Ninth Schedule is expressly protected from being struck down for inconsistency with the fundamental rights, though since the Coelho ruling such a law can still be tested against the basic structure, and the legislature remains free to repeal or amend it.

value: Only the first statement, that the roads were not always straight or exactly at right angles
reasoning: Harappan settlements were broadly laid out on a grid, but excavation shows the streets curved and met at angles other than ninety degrees in many places. The uniformity of the bricks lay in their proportions of one to two to four rather than in their absolute size, and the bricks used in fortification walls were larger than those used in houses, as at Kalibangan.

value: Kurinchi-mountainous, Palai-arid, Neytal-seashore, Mullai-pastoral
reasoning: The five tinai of Sangam poetry name landscapes: kurinchi the hills, mullai the pastoral woodland, marutam the cultivated plains, neytal the seacoast and palai the parched wasteland.

value: Only the statement that the Election Commission makes delimitation laws is wrong
reasoning: Parliament enacts the Delimitation Act and a separate Delimitation Commission redraws constituency boundaries under it; the Election Commission's charge of the electoral rolls, the Model Code taking effect on announcement of the schedule, and the bar on questioning an election except by election petition are all correct.

value: The claim that reports go only to the Lok Sabha is incorrect
reasoning: The Commission reports to the President, who causes the reports to be laid before both Houses of Parliament, and any part relating to a State goes to that State's Governor to be placed before its legislature.

value: A freedom guaranteed to citizens only
reasoning: The right to form associations or unions is one of the freedoms in Article 19(1), and the whole of Article 19 is conferred on citizens alone, subject to reasonable restrictions.

value: By amending the First Schedule through Parliament's constituent power
reasoning: Ceding Indian territory to another country cannot be done by executive agreement or ordinary law, as the Berubari opinion settled, so the Land Boundary Agreement was given effect by a constitutional amendment altering the First Schedule; that amendment did not fall within the categories requiring ratification by the State legislatures.
